Definition: Ammon, a son of Lot; also his posterity and their country
BiblicalUsage: Ammon, the son of Lot by his younger daughter, and his people are Israel's neighbours and enemies for a thousand years. Ben-ammi, the son of my people, is the father of the children of Ammon unto this day; Moses is told not to distress them, for God has given their land to the children of Lot for a possession; and Jephthah sends messengers to the king of the children of Ammon, asking what he has to do with him, that he comes to fight in his land.
TheologicalSignificance: The children of Lot are given their land by God and still come to fight for it, and that long neighbourhood is the whole story: Israel is told to leave them alone, and they will not leave Israel alone.
